newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand says more finance rescue packages on way.
newsitem.headline: Thailand says more finance rescue packages on way.

text.p: Thailand's central bank said on Thursday that it would announce more rescue packages for the troubled finance sector in a day or two to clear concerns about the sector.

"They should be announced in a day or two. These will be action plans to stabilise the finance sector and they will go into more details," Bank of Thailand chief economist Kleo-thong Hetrakul told reporters.

"My understanding is that they (rescue packages) would clear all concerns and misunderstanding about the finance sector and will enable people to better understand what we are going to do with financial institutions," she said.
"The public need not be panicked as the Bank of Thailand is well prepared to handle any plan or situation," she added.

Financial markets have been waiting anxiously to see what kind of rescue measures the authorities might be planning for ailing Thai financial institutions hit by massive loan overexposure to the depressed property sector.
The poor asset quality of banks and finance firms has been weighing heavily on the stock market, which is now at eight year lows, with investors reluctant to invest in their shares.

There has also been market talk that some of the weaker finance companies among the 91 in the country, hit by a liquidity crunch, might fold if they did not merge with bigger counterparts on their own accord or were forced to enter into mergers by the authorities.

On Wednesday, a senior government source told Reuters that debt-ridden Finance One Plc which used to be the top finance company in the country, was in new merger talks with Krungthai Thanakit Finance and Securities.

Finance One failed last month to carry through a much touted mega merger with Thai Danu Bank to create a new bank after tax and legal complications as well as the finance company's large debts came in the way.
Thai authorities who had blessed the failed deal then said that more steps would be announced in future to facilitate consolidation and mergers in the troubled finance sector.

On Tuesday, the cabinet issued urgent decrees to allow mergers in the finance sector and also liberalised foreign ownership limits -- now set at 25 percent -- for banks and finance firms that emerge from the moves.
